RobotBody.use: A friendly violet/teal humanoid robot (about 700 px tall, centred) that shows how a robot's brain, skills or training data get into its body. Pick the mode that matches the story beat.

props.mode: brain_drop (a glowing pink brain falls from the top into the robot's head on reveal; the visor lights up on impact) | lag (the head glows bright while the arms tremble stiffly and the robot leans; on reveal three tall walls rise in front of it, impact = walls land) | cards (small cards fly from the edges into the head one by one after reveal; the head glows more with each) | puzzle (three jigsaw pieces slide together from three sides and lock into the chest; a check mark on impact) | fleet (2-5 different robots in a row, single arm, dual arm and a four-legged dog, linked by light beams; each has a skill bar that rises after reveal)
props.items: list of 1-5 short Chinese labels for cards mode (default ["杯子","毛巾","门把手"]) or puzzle mode (default ["常识","手感","练习"], 3 items)
props.walls: list of up to 3 short Chinese labels for lag mode (default ["数据","动作","练习"])
props.count: fleet mode only: number of robots, integer 2-5 (default 3)

RobotBody.beats: reveal starts the change (brain falls, walls rise, cards fly, pieces slide in, skill bars rise). impact lands it (visor lights, walls land, check mark pops, squash).

Sim2Real.use: Simulation versus reality for sim-to-real explainers: a small room card (table, cube, lamp) drawn as a flat cyan-violet SIM wireframe and as a warm, soft-shadowed REAL room.

props.mode: grid (a 5x6 wall of tiny SIM rooms, each with a tiny robot arm moving out of phase; cells pop in quickly) | gap (SIM card left, REAL card right; on reveal a jagged crack opens between them with a red pill '现实差距') | randomize (one SIM room whose table colour, wall colour, lamp angle and camera tilt jump every 0.35 s, with a counter '花样 ×N' counting up) | transfer (the randomize flicker continues; on reveal a REAL room slides in; on impact a detection box snaps onto the cube with a green check and an optional error ruler) | doors (a chef walks through 4 coloured doors left to right and arrives at a normal home kitchen card on impact)
props.error: transfer mode only: the error label next to the detection box (default "1.5 cm"; an empty string hides the ruler and label)

Sim2Real.beats: reveal: the crack opens (gap), the REAL room slips in (transfer), or the walk ends at the door (doors). impact: the detection box snaps on with a check (transfer), or the kitchen card pops in (doors).

DataScale.use: Magnitudes of robot training data as a visual: a pile of text blocks, an ocean with a cupped hand, a fleet of robots with a calendar, a world map of dots, or a slow counter.

props.mode: mountain (many small text-line blocks pile up into a mountain; a big number pops above it) | ocean (a wide wavy ocean on the left with a tiny cupped hand holding a little water on the right; the hand highlights on reveal) | fleet (13 identical small arm robots in two rows, with a calendar that flips through months; label '13 台 · 17 个月' is built from count and months) | map (a stylised world map; glowing dots converge into a stacked counter on reveal) | counter (a small robot arm doing a grab, and a big counter at right that goes up by 1 about every 0.8 s)
props.label: big label text for mountain (default "15T+"), ocean (default "15 万亿"), map (default "100 万+ 条 · 22 种"), counter (default "网上搜不到"). Keep it short (up to about 14 characters)
props.small: ocean mode only: the small label under the hand (default "机器人数据")
props.count: fleet mode only: number of robots (default 13)
props.months: fleet mode only: the calendar flips up to this month (default 17)
props.start: counter mode only: the starting integer (default 0)

DataScale.beats: mountain, ocean, map: the pile, water or dots build from entrance; reveal triggers the highlight or convergence; impact pops the label. fleet: the calendar flips from reveal to impact. counter: ticks up continuously from entrance.
